ideas.title: Tides
ideas.critique: A world-level cycle that reshapes the coast every day is a real change in how the island works, not another event; it is the nearest thing to new here. Overlap is only the slow persistent change of terrain (Paths we wore) and the collect-things gathering; it risks being just a water-height slider unless the creatures really use it.

ideas.title: Lumi reads you its diary
ideas.critique: Lumi already reads a letter aloud and has voice, so a spoken text addressed to the visitor is close to a repeat. Generating it from the real log is a nice honest touch, but it is audio over nothing the player sees, and the human predicted this sort of thing in goal 5.

ideas.title: Island radio
ideas.critique: Spoken output plus friends gathering and reacting to a trigger repeats the Our song / letter recipe. The news built from the real event log, with creatures reacting to their own names, is a good twist but sits in the same sound-layer form.

ideas.title: I molt
ideas.critique: A lasting, comic change to Lumi's own body over an hour, with feathers left in the world, is a new kind of change: the character itself goes through a state. Lumi-centred, so it is close to the gag-film shape if staged as one scene, but the hour-long regrowth sets it apart.

ideas.title: A stranger washes ashore
ideas.critique: A species the island has never had, who shy friends must get to know over days, changes who lives here; it is the biggest idea in the round. New bodies have been done (New coats, Real claws), but a newcomer with its own behaviour and a relationship arc has not.

ideas.title: A map of us
ideas.critique: Drawing the island from logged movements reuses the frame-log data of Paths we wore, and the result is a document or picture, not play. Pleasant and field-guide-like, but a human who knows goal 5 could predict it.

ideas.title: The island tips
ideas.critique: A global physics rule driven by where the crowd stands is a genuinely new mechanic, so creatures' own behaviour changes the world and the world answers. Pumpkin and hail physics exist, but nothing couples crowd position to the whole island.

ideas.title: Night lasts until you come
ideas.critique: Holding the clock for the visitor inverts how the island works and is bold, though it hangs on the same browser-presence trigger as Someone's watching. Risk: it looks like a stuck night to anyone not checking.

ideas.title: Echoes
ideas.critique: A call-and-response gag with friends reacting is the Our song shape again, and the echo joke is predictable. The wrong-echo wordplay that grows bolder is charming but small.

ideas.title: Leftovers
ideas.critique: Persistent clutter found again later fits the slow-accumulating scenery form of Paths we wore and The gallery. The reunion with a lost bow gives it a story payoff, which lifts it above plain scenery.
